definition: Reorganization is a restructuring of the ownership, legal, operational, or financial arrangement of a business. It may occur outside bankruptcy through a merger or consolidation, recapitalization, spin-off, asset transfer, debt restructuring, or change in corporate form. A business may reorganize to address financial distress, change ownership or control, separate business lines, improve operations, or pursue a different strategy. Because the term is used in corporate, tax, and bankruptcy law, the legal consequences depend on the context. Under federal income tax law, Internal Revenue Code § 368 identifies several categories of corporate reorganization, including statutory mergers or consolidations; certain acquisitions of another corporation's stock or assets; certain transfers followed by qualifying distributions; recapitalizations; changes in a corporation's identity, form, or place of organization; and certain transfers in a Title 11 or similar case. If all applicable requirements are satisfied, related provisions, including Internal Revenue Code § 354 and Internal Revenue Code § 361, may provide nonrecognition of gain or loss for certain exchanges by shareholders, security holders, or participating corporations. Not every business restructuring qualifies under § 368, and qualification does not necessarily make every part of a transaction tax-free. In bankruptcy law, Chapter 11 generally provides a process for reorganization. It is commonly used by businesses, although individuals may also be eligible. The debtor ordinarily remains in control as a debtor in possession unless a trustee is appointed. A Chapter 11 plan generally must designate classes of claims and interests, identify impaired classes and their treatment, and provide adequate means for implementation. A plan may retain, transfer, or sell property; merge or consolidate the debtor with another entity; modify liens or debt instruments; cure defaults; extend maturity dates or change interest rates; issue securities; and assume, reject, or assign executory contracts or unexpired leases.
